_comment: sim-pick-contact-seal-fallback-v1 handoff. HOST-config keys (the block read by scripts/twin/restock_manipulation/ros_host.py -> TransferController) for the next complete restock run. They make the collect PICK contact phase either seal reliably or fail by name immediately, instead of coldwin63's silent 20 mm over-press that could never latch. All keys are OPT-IN and default off => absent block == byte-identical. config_preflight registers them as HOST, so a key filed in the RUNTIME config is REFUSED (not silently inert). Merge the keys below into the HOST config and REQUIRE them on the preflight (--require) for coldwin64.
_root_cause: coldwin63's pick never sealed NOT because the controller skipped suction, but because its ONE-SHOT gripper-enable control was LOST in delivery. The controller runs in the host subprocess: host-stack.log:2540 shows it DID issue 'CONTACT_SUCTION enable' and then pressed six CONTACT_STEP advances (3..18 mm) to HOST_FAULT_ESTOP 'contact not reached within capped over-press travel' (host-stack.log:4675). The enable reaches the Isaac plugin ONLY via the /manipulation/status 'controls' field, relayed by scripts/twin/restock/control_ipc.py HostControlPublisher, which keeps ONLY the latest payload per topic (a last-value relay, control_ipc.py:156-180). A later heartbeat / empty-controls status (the StatusHeartbeat filler + the controller's own next empty emit) overwrote the single control-bearing status before scripts/twin/restock_manipulation/isaac_ros_graph.py IsaacRosGraph.poll (lines 262-294) read it; poll's `sequence <= last_sequence` gate then dropped it and advanced past it, so scripts/twin/restock_manipulation/cad_tool.py NativePanelContact.command(close) was NEVER called -> plugin stayed status=Open enabled=False (console: 959 reads, 0 'SEAL_DIAG command:close') -> the gated SIM_ATTACH_FALLBACK stayed skip=suction_off -> contact never formed -> the over-press cap fault. coldwin62/coldwin61 WON the race (console:4881 'SEAL_DIAG command:close' BEFORE contact); cw63 lost it (its 22 vs 9 pre-grasp 'suction_off' ticks ARE the larger overwrite window the integration note flagged). Reconstruction pinned on CPU; the single-shot drop and the re-emit fix are proven through the REAL IsaacRosGraph.poll + a faithful last-value relay in scripts/twin/tests/test_pick_contact_seal_fallback.py.
_contact_reissue_suction_each_tick_note: ITEM-2 fix, the one to turn on for coldwin64. Re-publishes the gripper-enable control on EVERY contact-press tick (running ticks and the freeze-settle holds) until the seal forms, so the last-value /manipulation/status relay ALWAYS carries a fresh control when the mission polls -- the single-shot enable can no longer be overwritten and dropped. Idempotent (close_gripper is re-called harmlessly, exactly as coldwin62 already applied command:close twice). Behaviour-preserving for the sealed runs (the seal still forms); off => the historical single emit (byte-identical).
_contact_require_suction_enabled_note: GUARD 3a. At the first over-press step (after the freeze-settle), if the plugin never reported enabled/closing, do NOT keep pressing into the carton with no chance of a latch: fail fast 'CONTACT_SUCTION_NOT_ENABLED at over-press step N (...)' with the SEAL_DIAG fields. Satisfies the captain's 'fail by name immediately instead of pressing 0.02 m with no chance of a latch'. Needs the Isaac-side feedback (Sensors.gripper_enabled, populated by the driver from the plugin status).
_contact_reissue_close_once_note: Sub-option of require_suction_enabled: on the FIRST not-enabled over-press boundary, re-send the close command ONCE and hold for a second settle instead of failing; a SECOND miss then fails CONTACT_SUCTION_NOT_ENABLED. A belt-and-braces recovery for a single lost enable even if reissue_suction_each_tick is off.
_contact_accept_seal_diag_note: GUARD 3b. When the geometric SEAL_DIAG shows the pad flush on a body under the pad (seal_gap_mm <= contact_seal_diag_max_gap_mm, seal_pad_angle_deg <= contact_seal_diag_max_angle_deg, a body under the pad) for contact_seal_diag_dwell_ticks consecutive ticks AND suction is enabled, treat it as contact: drive the SAME contact-termination the plugin latch drives (the gated SIM_ATTACH_FALLBACK forms the weld Isaac-side; this never invents a new attach mechanism). Logs 'CONTACT_SOURCE_DISAGREE plugin=False seal_diag=True ...' once. A geometric backstop for a plugin latch that is slow/flaky when the pad is provably flush.
_seal_diag_bounds_note: Defaults match the native SIM_ATTACH weld gate class (sub-mm flush, ~a degree). The dwell requires a STABLE seal (not a one-tick flicker) before accepting.
_expected_pass_coldwin64: The collect pick logs 'SEAL_DIAG command:close' on the mission console within the first over-press tick (never 959 reads with status=Open), the native plugin and/or the gated SIM_ATTACH_FALLBACK forms the weld, and collect reports SUCCEEDED (seal + lift). If the plugin genuinely cannot seal, the run fails fast with a NAMED reason ('CONTACT_SUCTION_NOT_ENABLED ...' or the seal-diag diagnostic) and NO 'contact not reached within capped over-press travel' after a full 20 mm press, and NO opaque 'arm command heartbeat lost'.
_minimal_set_if_conservative: If only ONE key is wanted first, enable contact_reissue_suction_each_tick alone -- it directly addresses the observed cw63 delivery loss and makes the pick seal reliably; it needs no Sensors feedback plumbing. Add require_suction_enabled (+reissue_close_once) and accept_seal_diag as defence-in-depth.
_out_of_scope: Nothing in preplace/place/transfer, gripper geometry, carton size, or the real robot was touched. The side-grasp standoff over-reach is a separate concern (sim-collect-press-regression-v1); this lane is purely the contact-phase seal/latch delivery + guards.
